sources.name: CO-OPS Data API: tide predictions every 6 minutes, on mean sea level, in GMT
sources.by: NOAA Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services. Every request and response is in /tides/sources/noaa.jsonl

sources.name: CO-OPS Data API: high and low tide predictions (interval=hilo)
sources.by: NOAA CO-OPS. Leaves out a high and a low less than about 2 hours apart; no case depends on one

sources.name: CO-OPS Metadata API: harmonic constituents (harcon.json), metric
sources.by: NOAA CO-OPS. Amplitude in metres, phase_GMT as phaseInDegrees

sources.name: XTide 2.16 on the same constants
sources.by: David Flater. Its equilibrium arguments and node factors are congen's, from SP 98. Within 0.004 m and 60 s of every case it checks; it blends one year into the next over the hour either side of 1 January, so it doesn't check those. Every call is in /tides/sources/xtide.txt

sources.name: Manual of Harmonic Analysis and Prediction of Tides, Special Publication 98, 1958 reprint: tables 2, 2a, 14 and 15
sources.by: Paul Schureman, US Coast and Geodetic Survey. The method to follow; no value in the file comes from it

sources.name: Tidal Analysis and Prediction, NOAA Special Publication NOS CO-OPS 3, 2007, section 2.2.4
sources.by: Bernard D. Parker. One node factor and one u per year, both for the middle of the year

operations.gives: The predicted height at an instant
The next high and the next low after an instant

fields.constituents: A station's harmonic constants: a list of objects, each with name, amplitudeInMeters and phaseInDegrees. The cases give NOAA's published set for a station in NOAA's order, leaving out those with zero amplitude.
fields.name: In each constituent: its name as NOAA spells it, one of NOAA's 37: M2, S2, N2, K1, M4, O1, M6, MK3, S4, MN4, NU2, S6, MU2, 2N2, OO1, LAM2, S1, M1, J1, MM, SSA, SA, MSF, MF, RHO, Q1, T2, R2, 2Q1, P1, 2SM2, M3, L2, 2MK3, K2, M8, MS4. Any other name is invalidInput.
fields.amplitudeInMeters: In each constituent: its mean amplitude H, 0 or more. NOAA gives the millimetre.
fields.phaseInDegrees: In each constituent: its Greenwich phase lag κ′ (NOAA's phase_GMT), 0 to 360. NOAA gives a tenth of a degree.
fields.startUtc: The instant to search from, ISO 8601 with Z
fields.heightInMeters: The height above the constituents' mean, which for NOAA's sets is mean sea level: the sum of the constituents, with no constant term. NOAA gives the millimetre.
fields.highUtc: The first high water after startUtc: the first local maximum of the predicted height. NOAA gives the minute.
fields.highHeightInMeters: The predicted height at highUtc, as heightInMeters
fields.lowUtc: The first low water after startUtc: the first local minimum. A low that comes before the high is still the first low.
fields.lowHeightInMeters: The predicted height at lowUtc, as heightInMeters
